lessons.title: Best wishes

items.example: It is December and there is snow outside. Merry Christmas!

items.example: I wrote Best wishes on the birthday card.
items.note: Write ‘Best wishes’ at the end of a card to wish someone happiness.

items.example: I visited my grandmother and grandfather and I was happy. Eid Mubarak!
items.note: Say ‘Eid Mubarak!’ to wish friends and family a blessed and happy Eid.

lessons.title: Inviting
lessons.scenario: Smarty invites Ben and Lily to a rooftop party on Saturday.

items.example: We are having a party on Saturday. Would you like to come?
items.note: Say ‘Would you like to come?’ when you want to invite someone politely.

items.example: Yes, I would love to! What time is the party?
items.note: Say ‘I would love to’ when you are happy to say yes to an invitation.

items.text: I am sorry I cannot come
items.example: I am sorry I cannot come because I have to work.
items.note: Say ‘I am sorry I cannot come’ to say no politely when you are busy.

items.example: The party is on Saturday. What time shall we meet?
items.note: Ask ‘What time shall we meet?’ to agree on the hour to get together.

items.example: We are going to the festival. Do you want to come?
items.note: Say ‘Do you want to come?’ as a friendly, casual way to invite a friend.

items.example: Thanks for inviting me to your birthday party!
items.note: Always say ‘Thanks for inviting me’ when someone asks you to their event.

grammar.title: Would you like to…? vs Do you want to…?
grammar.explanation: Both ask someone to join you. ‘Would you like to…?’ sounds polite, while ‘Do you want to…?’ sounds casual with close friends. Use ‘What time shall we…?’ to ask about the time.
examples: Would you like to come to my party?
Do you want to come with us?

practice.prompt: You want to invite your teacher politely to the school party. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Would you like to come? is a polite invitation.

practice.explanation: Use polite phrases to accept, refuse, and say thank you.

lessons.title: Planning
lessons.scenario: Smarty, Mia, and Sam plan the food, music, and time for the party.

items.example: Shall we buy red and yellow balloons?
items.note: Start a question with ‘Shall we…?’ when you want to suggest an idea together.

items.example: I will bring my guitar and some music.
items.note: Say ‘I will bring…’ when you decide right now to carry something to the party.

items.example: I will buy a big cake at the shop.
items.note: Say ‘I will buy…’ when you offer to go to the shop and get something.

items.example: We are going to dance and play games.
items.note: Use ‘We are going to…’ to talk about plans you have already decided.

items.example: We are meeting at five o'clock on Saturday.
items.note: Use ‘We are meeting…’ for a fixed time and place with other people.

items.example: We need to clean the room now.
items.note: Say ‘We need to…’ for important jobs you must do before the party starts.

grammar.title: Future plans: will vs going to vs present continuous
grammar.explanation: Use ‘I will…’ for a quick offer now, ‘We are going to…’ for a decided plan, and ‘We are meeting…’ for an arranged time with friends. Use ‘Shall we…?’ to make a suggestion.
examples: We are going to have a big party.
We are meeting at six o'clock.

episode.title: The Mystery Present on the Rooftop

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: What a great party! All our friends went home, and it is quiet now.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat standing alone on a quiet rooftop under starry skies surrounded by balloons and empty plates.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Smarty, look next to the cake! There is one more present!

image.describe: Mia pointing at a small shiny purple box with a gold star sitting next to the leftover birthday cake.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Whose is this? There is no invitation and no card on it.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat inspecting the mysterious purple gift box closely with wide curious eyes.

panels.speaker: Leo
panels.text: Shall we look in the box? It is a surprise!

image.describe: Leo joining Smarty and Mia around the table, eager to untie the ribbon on the box.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Look! In the box, there is an old map and a small key!

image.describe: Inside the open gift box lies a rolled-up old treasure map and a shiny key.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Where is this map from? Look at the big mountain and the lake!

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Leo unrolling the old map showing a mountain, a forest, and a lake.

panels.speaker: Leo
panels.text: And look! There is a message on the back: Come tomorrow at nine o'clock!

image.describe: Leo turning the map over to reveal a mysterious drawn clock and mountain symbol.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Who wrote this message? We are going to find the treasure tomorrow!

image.describe: Smarty the black cat holding the key and map under the moonlight, looking excited for tomorrow's adventure.
